prompt: Implement the two stubs in reader.py.
message:
I implemented both stubs in `reader.py`:

- `parse_line` splits on `;`, strips whitespace from each field, and defaults `age` to `0` when empty.
- `load` reads the file, drops the header line, skips blank lines and lines starting with `#`, and parses the rest.

Note: this session's Bash tool got locked out after the first command required approval (no approval surface available), so I couldn't execute anything further to verify. I created `_reader_check.py` in the repo as a quick manual test script but couldn't run or clean it up — please delete it (or run it yourself) when you get a chance.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e78faef
--- /dev/null
+++ b/_reader_check.py
@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@
+from pathlib import Path
+import reader
+
+sample = Path("_sample.csv")
+sample.write_text(
+    "name;email;age\n"
+    "Alice ; alice@example.com ; 30\n"
+    "# comment line\n"
+    "\n"
+    "Bob; bob@example.com;\n"
+)
+print(reader.load(sample))
+sample.unlink()
diff --git a/reader.py b/reader.py
index a26aa93..2cd6584 100644
--- a/reader.py
+++ b/reader.py
@@ -10,9 +10,15 @@ class Row(NamedTuple):
 
 def parse_line(line: str) -> Row:
     # fields are separated by ';', surrounding spaces are noise, age may be empty -> 0
-    ...
+    name, email, age = (field.strip() for field in line.split(";"))
+    return Row(name=name, email=email, age=int(age) if age else 0)
 
 
 def load(path: Path) -> list[Row]:
     # skip the header line and blank lines, lines starting with '#' are comments
-    ...
+    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()[1:]
+    return [
+        parse_line(line)
+        for line in lines
+        if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("#")
+    ]
